Problem Statement
Problem: Algorithms - 23
Suppose G is a flow network containing two feasible (s, t)-flows, denoted by f and g,
satisfying the condition |g| > |f|. Prove that the residual network Gf admits a feasible
(s, t)-flow with a value equal to |g| −|f|.

0002 | **Solution:** Let f and g be two feasible (s, t)-flows on G with |g| > |f|. We
0003 | construct a flow h in the residual network Gf such that |h| = |g| −|f|. Recall that in Gf,
0004 | each original edge (u, v) yields a **forward residual arc** (u, v) with capacity cf(u, v) =
0005 | c(u, v) −f(u, v) and a **backward residual arc** (v, u) with capacity cf(v, u) = f(u, v).
0006 | Define h : E(Gf) →R≥0 as follows: for each original edge (u, v) in G, compare the flows
0007 | g(u, v) and f(u, v):
0008 | - If g(u, v) ≥f(u, v), assign
0009 | h(u, v) := g(u, v) −f(u, v)
0010 | on the forward residual arc (u, v). - If g(u, v) < f(u, v), assign
0011 | h(v, u) := f(u, v) −g(u, v)
0012 | on the backward residual arc (v, u).
0013 | In all other cases (if an arc exists in Gf but is not assigned by the above), let h be 0.
0014 | Intuitively, h “pushes” the excess flow of g over f along each edge if g exceeds f there, or
0015 | in the reverse direction if f exceeds g. We will show that h is a feasible (s, t)-flow in Gf of
0016 | value |g| −|f|.
0017 | **(i) Capacity constraints:** For any original edge (u, v), if h(u, v) = g(u, v) −f(u, v) as
0018 | above, then 0 ≤h(u, v) by construction, and moreover
0019 | h(u, v) = g(u, v) −f(u, v) ≤c(u, v) −f(u, v) = cf(u, v),
0020 | since g(u, v) ≤c(u, v) (feasibility of g). Thus h(u, v) does not exceed the forward residual
0021 | capacity. Similarly, if h(v, u) = f(u, v) −g(u, v) is assigned on a backward arc, then
0022 | 0 ≤h(v, u) = f(u, v) −g(u, v) ≤f(u, v) = cf(v, u),
0023 | using g(u, v) ≥0. So h(v, u) respects the backward residual capacity. All other arcs carry
0024 | h = 0, trivially within capacity. Therefore 0 ≤h(e) ≤cf(e) for every residual arc e, i.e. h
0025 | satisfies all capacity constraints in Gf.

0027 | in Gf. This follows from the flow-conservation of f and g on the original network. Indeed,
